stem: Meena buys a packet of salt from the market. The label on the packet says "100% pure salt", but it also lists sodium chloride and a small amount of an anti-caking agent as its contents. Her Science teacher asks: In the scientific sense, what is this salt?

options.text: A pure substance, because the label says it is 100% pure
A mixture, because it contains more than one kind of substance
An element, because it contains only one kind of atom
A compound, because all mixtures are compounds

teacher.key_rationale: The packet contains sodium chloride plus an anti-caking agent, so more than one substance is present. Scientifically, a material with more than one substance mixed together is a mixture, regardless of the everyday claim 'pure' on the label. Option A is the trap for a student who applies the everyday (consumer-label) meaning of pure instead of the scientific definition.
